title: PlugMem — where the paper and the code part ways
subtitle: Only the 14 divergences confirmed in verification.md §5. Each node states both sides; edges are omitted — this graph is a checklist, not a pipeline.
source: paper arXiv:2603.03296v1  ×  repo PlugMem @ 3b2ce75   ·   servers/plugmem/verification.md §5, 15 divergences found; D15 (a documentation-dating error about the plugmem/ package's git history, not a flow divergence) excluded here
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ code divergence
legend_notes: D1 is the structural headline: the paper's default multi-hop loop (B8) has no system-side counterpart at all — the nearest code analog is an external, opt-in, semantic-only eval script (HotpotQA only, off by default).

Three of the fourteen divergences share one shape — a real signal is computed and then thrown away: return score (D2, forced to 0.0), importance (D4, forced to 0), and the 'only one memory type' router (D11, contradicts the paper's own Table 14).

D7's promotion pathway (credibility/confidence/coding-assistant memory promotion) is the single biggest code-only addition — a whole fourth write channel with no paper counterpart, entered via a separate API and bypassing every other node in this diagram.
